results.summary: up/down never drop a pid file without a fresh, guarded re-read confirming it's dead, right before the delete. down's "not running" tidy and up's dead-at-recheck tidy now share dropDeadPidFile(root, name, deps) in src/up.js, which re-reads the pid file immediately before rmSync instead of trusting the processState/liveness snapshot the caller already acted on -- a concurrent hkb up (or the process's own claimServePid/acquireLoopLock) rewriting the file to a live pid in that window now survives both tidy paths. up now also tidies serve.pid for the corpse it just reported failed at the SPAWN_CHECK_MS recheck, guarded the same way and gated on still owning the claim (claimPid's return value). down's stale-pid-file line now says "removed" when it actually removed the file, instead of reusing --status's read-only "hkb up replaces it" wording. deadAtRecheck (src/model.js) now returns {line, failed} directly instead of a flat {name,pid,log,line} shape up.js re-picked apart into three fields; added a direct unit test in test/model.test.js. docs/wiki/features/up-and-down.md was re-verified and re-stamped: every src/up.js/model.js/dispatch.js line anchor had drifted (both from #164's merge and from #162's continuation-review merge landing mid-task), and Known limits gained a bullet about the 300ms SPAWN_CHECK_MS recheck window (a child that dies just after it is still reported started, exit 0).
